fixes.explanation: I get why you'd think so, friend, but the text says something else. The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, hears Israel is coming along the road to Atharim, and "he attacked Israel and captured some prisoners." (Numbers 21:1). I think this part hurts, because real people were taken. So the answer is False, since he attacked.

That's it, baker! The text says the king of Arad hears Israel is coming along the road to Atharim, and he attacks Israel (Numbers 21:1). He's a Canaanite king who lived in the Negev. So the answer is False. He attacked, and he captured some prisoners.

Good guess, since treasure is what we expect in a story like this. But this passage never mentions gold or silver. The only thing it says the king took is that he attacked Israel and "captured some prisoners." (Numbers 21:1). So prisoners is the answer that matches the text.

YES, baker! After the attack, the text says "So Israel made a vow to the LORD" (Numbers 21:2). They brought it to Him. Me, I'd have probably started by panicking at full volume. Israel makes a promise to the LORD.

Altars are a fair guess, friend, since they're a big part of worship. But this passage never says Israel builds one. What it says is that Israel "made a vow to the LORD" (Numbers 21:2). A vow is a promise spoken to Him, and that's the answer here.

Sending spies is a smart-sounding move, friend. But this passage never says Israel sends any into Arad. After the attack, the text says Israel "made a vow to the LORD" (Numbers 21:2). That's what Israel does here.

That's the one, baker. Israel says, "If You will deliver this people into our hands…" (Numbers 21:2). Notice how the vow starts with "If." They're asking the LORD to deliver the people, and they attach a promise of their own to the request. The vow then goes on to say, "we will devote their cities to destruction."

You got it, baker! In the vow, Israel said, "we will devote their cities to destruction." (Numbers 21:2). Then the LORD delivered up the Canaanites, and the text says "Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction" (Numbers 21:3). They said it, and then they did it. This is a heavy part, but the text is clear that the vow was kept.

That's a fair worry, since promises get broken all the time. I've promised to eat just one cookie more than once. But Israel doesn't break this one. The vow was to "devote their cities to destruction" (Numbers 21:2), and the text says "Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction" (Numbers 21:3).

Putting things off is very human, friend. I've been putting off cleaning my oven for ages. But the text doesn't mention any delay here. It says the LORD delivered up the Canaanites, and "Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction" (Numbers 21:3). So they kept the vow.

Perfect, baker! The text says "so they named the place Hormah." (Numbers 21:3). That comes right after the LORD heard Israel's plea and delivered up the Canaanites. It's also the title of this whole lesson. Hormah is the name Israel gave the place.

Meribah sounds like a real contender, friend, so I see why it caught your eye. But it's not the name in this passage. After the LORD delivers up the Canaanites, the text says "so they named the place Hormah." (Numbers 21:3). The answer is Hormah.
Kadesh has a good ring to it, so I see where that came from. But it's not the name Israel gives here. The text says "so they named the place Hormah." (Numbers 21:3). The answer is Hormah.
